svg.text: BEST FOR: HARNESS² DUAL-LOOP SELF-IMPROVING AGENTS
FORMAT LINEAGE: Gurisa Roy (#02, 201 likes) • Keith R. Worfolk (#03) • Google & Northwestern Harness²
Google Harness²: How Recursive Self-Improving Harnesses Beat Static Agents Without Retraining Weights
Most 'agent failures' are harness failures. Harness² adds two recursive loops around a frozen model: Task-Level Skill Graphs and Harness-Level Evolution.
Analyze the user goal and current workspace state; propose
a candidate DAG of modular skills and explicit
Run candidate sub-skills inside an isolated gVisor / E2B
container; capture deterministic exit codes, stderr
Discard failing branches, repair broken tool arguments
from probe feedback, and compose the verified sub-skills
Static harnesses hardcode one prompt template, one tool
list, and one retry rule for every task. When an
enterprise workflow hits an unfamiliar schema or multi-
step edge case, a static harness repeats the same broken
COMPLETE 6-STEP HARNESS EXECUTION LOOP (01 -> 06, ZERO SKIPPED STEPS)
Cluster failed steps across production trajectories by error signature.
Generate targeted edit to SKILL.md, tool schema, or guardrail code.
Reject patches that grow prompt >15% or hardcode benchmark answers.
Promote only if peak score rises AND 100% of golden fixtures pass.
VERIFIED HARNESS² BENCHMARK GAINS (SAME BASE MODEL)
Upgrading the model while keeping a brittle harness yields
diminishing returns. Making the harness itself recursive —
proposing, probing, and composing skills per task while
evolving instructions across tasks — unlocks +4.5 to +11.8
points on the exact same frozen model.
Rule: Freeze the model weights, evolve the harness — Loop 1 adapts the skill graph per task; Loop 2 promotes verified patches across tasks.
